stem.en: The innermost wall layer of a microsporangium, which nourishes developing pollen grains, is the:

explanation.en: The tapetum is the innermost layer; its cells are dense, often multinucleate, and nourish the developing pollen.

stem.en: The exine of the pollen grain is made of:

explanation.en: Exine is sporopollenin, which resists high temperature, strong acids and alkalis; the intine is cellulose and pectin.

stem.en: A typical angiosperm anther has how many microsporangia?

explanation.en: A bilobed, dithecous anther has two microsporangia in each lobe, four in all.

stem.en: Pollen grains of rice and wheat lose viability within about:

explanation.en: NCERT notes that rice and wheat pollen lose viability within 30 minutes; some Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae pollen stay viable for months.

solution.en: NCERT notes that rice and wheat pollen lose viability within 30 minutes; some Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae pollen stay viable for months.

stem.en: In a plant with 2n = 16, the number of chromosomes in the vegetative cell of a pollen grain is:

explanation.en: The vegetative cell comes from a haploid microspore by mitosis, so it has n = 8.

stem.en: The mature embryo sac of a typical angiosperm is:

explanation.en: Eight nuclei form, but the two polar nuclei lie in one central cell, giving 7 cells.

stem.en: The filiform apparatus is found in the:

explanation.en: The synergids have cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which guide the pollen tube.

stem.en: The development of an embryo sac from a single megaspore is called:

explanation.en: When one of the four megaspores forms the embryo sac, the development is monosporic.

stem.en: The ploidy of the nucellus, synergids and antipodals of an ovule is respectively:

explanation.en: The nucellus is maternal sporophytic tissue (2n); synergids and antipodals are cells of the haploid embryo sac (n).

solution.en: The nucellus is maternal sporophytic tissue (2n); synergids and antipodals are cells of the haploid embryo sac (n).

stem.en: In an ovule, the body of the ovule fuses with the funicle in the region called the:

explanation.en: The hilum is the junction between the ovule and the funicle; the chalaza is the basal part opposite the micropyle.

stem.en: Which plant produces cleistogamous flowers?

explanation.en: Viola, Oxalis and Commelina bear both chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers.

stem.en: Geitonogamy is:

options.en: transfer of pollen to another flower of the same plant
transfer of pollen to a flower of another plant

explanation.en: Geitonogamy involves a pollinating agent but the pollen comes from the same plant, so it is genetically self-pollination.

stem.en: Which of these is pollinated by water?

explanation.en: Vallisneria, Hydrilla and the marine seagrass Zostera are water-pollinated; water lily and lotus are insect- or wind-pollinated.

stem.en: A dioecious plant such as papaya prevents:

explanation.en: Male and female flowers are on different plants, so only xenogamy is possible.

solution.en: Male and female flowers are on different plants, so only xenogamy is possible.

stem.en: Emasculation is required in artificial hybridisation when the female parent has:

explanation.en: Anthers must be removed from bisexual flowers to prevent self-pollination; unisexual female flowers need only bagging.

stem.en: Triple fusion in angiosperms is the fusion of:

options.en: a male gamete with the egg
two male gametes with the egg
a male gamete with a synergid
a male gamete with two polar nuclei

explanation.en: Triple fusion produces the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

stem.en: Coconut water from a tender coconut is:

explanation.en: The free-nuclear endosperm has thousands of nuclei; the surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm.

stem.en: Which of these is a non-albuminous seed?

explanation.en: In pea and groundnut the endosperm is used up by the embryo; wheat, maize and castor retain endosperm.

stem.en: In a plant with 2n = 14, the number of chromosomes in the endosperm cell is:

explanation.en: Endosperm is triploid: 3n = 3 × 7 = 21.

stem.en: The minimum number of meiotic divisions needed to produce 100 seeds in an angiosperm is:

explanation.en: 100 megaspore mother cell meioses for 100 eggs + 25 pollen mother cell meioses for 100 pollen grains = 125.

stem.en: Apomixis is the:

options.en: germination of pollen on the stigma
development of many embryos in a seed

explanation.en: Apomixis produces seeds asexually; fruit formation without fertilisation is parthenocarpy.

stem.en: Polyembryony from nucellar cells is commonly seen in:

explanation.en: Many Citrus and mango varieties form nucellar embryos.

stem.en: Nucellar embryos in a seed are:

options.en: genetically identical to the father plant
genetically identical to the mother plant

explanation.en: They arise from diploid maternal nucellus cells by mitosis, so they are clones of the mother.

stem.en: Why must farmers buy hybrid seed every year?

options.en: The F1 characters segregate in the next generation

explanation.en: Sexual reproduction of the heterozygous F1 leads to segregation; apomictic hybrids would avoid this.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous.
Reason (R): Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all, and their anthers and stigma lie close to each other.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Since the flower never opens, no foreign pollen can land on the stigma; pollen from its own anthers is the only option, so R explains A.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The endosperm of coconut is entirely cellular.
Reason (R): Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm made up of thousands of nuclei.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Coconut has both: the water is free-nuclear endosperm and the white kernel is cellular endosperm. So A is false and R is true.

passage.en: A plant breeder wants to cross two tomato varieties: variety A (high yield) as the female parent and variety B (disease resistant) as the male parent. Tomato flowers are bisexual. She opens the flower buds of variety A and removes their anthers with forceps before the anthers dehisce, then covers each bud with a butter-paper bag. When the stigmas become receptive, she dusts pollen collected from variety B on them and bags the flowers again.

stem.en: Why did the breeder remove the anthers while the flowers of variety A were still buds?

options.en: To prevent self-pollination of variety A
To stop the stigma from becoming receptive

explanation.en: Emasculation before dehiscence ensures that the stigma of the bisexual flower receives no pollen of its own, only the pollen of variety B.

passage.en: A plant breeder wants to cross two tomato varieties: variety A (high yield) as the female parent and variety B (disease resistant) as the male parent. Tomato flowers are bisexual. She opens the flower buds of variety A and removes their anthers with forceps before the anthers dehisce, then covers each bud with a butter-paper bag. When the stigmas become receptive, she dusts pollen collected from variety B on them and bags the flowers again.

stem.en: If the breeder repeated this cross using papaya (a dioecious plant) as the female parent, which step could she skip?

explanation.en: Female papaya flowers have no anthers, so emasculation is unnecessary; bagging is still needed to keep out unwanted pollen.

stem.en: Consider these statements about the wall of a microsporangium: (i) The tapetum is the innermost layer and nourishes the developing pollen. (ii) The endothecium lies just below the epidermis. (iii) The middle layers lie between the endothecium and the tapetum. (iv) The epidermis divides to form pollen grains. Which statements are correct?

explanation.en: The wall layers from outside in are epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum; the tapetum nourishes the pollen. Pollen grains come from the sporogenous tissue (pollen mother cells), not the epidermis, so (iv) is wrong.

solution.en: The wall layers from outside in are epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum; the tapetum nourishes the pollen.
Pollen grains come from the sporogenous tissue (pollen mother cells), not the epidermis, so (iv) is wrong.

stem.en: Match Column I with Column II. Column I: (a) Funicle (b) Hilum (c) Micropyle (d) Chalaza. Column II: (i) basal part of the ovule opposite the micropyle (ii) stalk that attaches the ovule to the placenta (iii) region where the body of the ovule fuses with the funicle (iv) small opening left by the integuments.

explanation.en: The funicle is the stalk; the hilum is where the ovule joins the funicle; the micropyle is the opening in the integuments; the chalaza is the basal part opposite the micropyle.

stem.en: Which of the following prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy?

options.en: Anther and stigma placed at different positions in a bisexual flower

explanation.en: In dioecious plants such as papaya, male and female flowers are on different plants, so neither autogamy nor geitonogamy can occur. Monoecy and different positions of anther and stigma stop only autogamy; cleistogamy ensures autogamy.

solution.en: In dioecious plants such as papaya, male and female flowers are on different plants, so neither autogamy nor geitonogamy can occur.
Monoecy and different positions of anther and stigma stop only autogamy; cleistogamy ensures autogamy.

stem.en: In a flowering plant with 2n = 24, what are the chromosome numbers of the endosperm, the embryo and the nucellus, respectively?

explanation.en: n = 12. Endosperm is triploid: 3 × 12 = 36. The embryo comes from the diploid zygote: 24. The nucellus is maternal diploid tissue: 24.

stem.en: Assertion (A): Nucellar embryos of Citrus are genetically identical to the mother plant. Reason (R): They develop from diploid cells of the nucellus without fertilisation.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

explanation.en: Nucellar cells are the mother plant's own diploid cells, and no gametes fuse, so the embryos formed from them are clones of the mother. R explains A.

stem.en: Which wall layer of the microsporangium nourishes the developing pollen grains?

explanation.en: The microsporangium wall has four layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum. The innermost layer, the tapetum, has cells with dense cytoplasm (often more than one nucleus) and nourishes the developing pollen grains. The outer three layers protect the sporangium and help in dehiscence of the anther to release pollen.

stem.en: A typical angiosperm anther is:

explanation.en: A typical anther is bilobed, each lobe has two theca, so it is dithecous. The anther is a tetragonal structure with four microsporangia, two in each lobe, located at its corners. 'Dithecous with two microsporangia' confuses theca with lobes.

stem.en:
Statement I: Germ pores are apertures on the pollen exine where sporopollenin is absent.
Statement II: The intine is a thin, continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin.

explanation.en: Both statements are NCERT facts. The exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent; the pollen tube emerges through them. The intine is thin and continuous, made of cellulose and pectin. Since both are true, option 1 is correct.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the:

explanation.en: In over 60% of angiosperms pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage (vegetative cell + generative cell). In the remaining species the generative cell divides mitotically before shedding to give two male gametes, i.e. the 3-celled stage.

stem.en: Which statement correctly describes the two cells of a mature 2-celled pollen grain?

explanation.en: The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small, spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus, and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell. Options 1 and 2 swap the two cells.

options.en: The generative cell is larger and stores abundant food reserves
The vegetative cell is small and spindle-shaped
The generative cell is small, spindle-shaped and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell
Both cells are of equal size and are separated by a cellulose wall

stem.en: Pollen grains of many species can be stored for years in pollen banks in liquid nitrogen at:

explanation.en: Liquid nitrogen boils at −196 °C; pollen cryopreserved at this temperature stays viable for years and is used in crop-breeding programmes. −273 °C is absolute zero, not a storage temperature.

stem.en: In which of the following do pollen grains lose viability within about 30 minutes of release?

explanation.en: Pollen viability varies with temperature and humidity. In rice and wheat pollen loses viability within about 30 minutes of release, whereas in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae it stays viable for months.

stem.en: Which weed, believed to have entered India as a contaminant with imported wheat, is a major cause of pollen allergy?

explanation.en: Parthenium (carrot grass) came into India as a contaminant with imported wheat. It has become ubiquitous and its pollen causes allergy and chronic respiratory disorders such as asthma and bronchitis. Eichhornia (water hyacinth) is an aquatic weed, not an allergen of this kind.

stem.en: What is the minimum number of meiotic divisions needed to produce 60 pollen grains and 60 female gametophytes (embryo sacs)?

explanation.en: One microspore mother cell gives a tetrad of 4 microspores (pollen) by one meiosis, so 60 pollen need 60/4 = 15 meioses. One megaspore mother cell gives 4 megaspores but only one is functional and forms an embryo sac, so 60 embryo sacs need 60 meioses. Total = 15 + 60 = 75. 120 counts one meiosis per pollen; 30 wrongly treats female meiosis like male.

stem.en:
Match the structure with its ploidy:
A. Nucellus
B. Primary endosperm nucleus
C. Antipodal cell
D. Zygote
I. n
II. 2n
III. 3n

explanation.en: The nucellus is sporophytic tissue of the ovule (2n). The PEN forms by fusion of a male gamete (n) with two polar nuclei (n + n), so it is 3n. Antipodals are cells of the haploid embryo sac (n). The zygote is male gamete + egg (2n). So A-II, B-III, C-I, D-II.

stem.en: The typical mature embryo sac of flowering plants is:

explanation.en: The mature embryo sac has 8 nuclei but 7 cells: 3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg cell and one large central cell holding the 2 polar nuclei. The central cell is binucleate, which is why there is one cell fewer than nuclei.

stem.en: The filiform apparatus, which guides the pollen tube, is present in the:

explanation.en: The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which plays an important role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid.

stem.en: Formation of the embryo sac from a single functional megaspore is called:

explanation.en: In most flowering plants only one of the four megaspores is functional, while the other three degenerate. Embryo sac formation from a single megaspore is termed monosporic development. Polyembryony is the presence of more than one embryo in a seed.

stem.en: The nucleus of the functional megaspore forms the 8-nucleate embryo sac by:

explanation.en: The functional megaspore nucleus divides mitotically to form 2 nuclei, which move to opposite poles; two more sequential divisions give 4 + 4 nuclei. That is 2³ = 8 nuclei from three divisions, and these are free-nuclear (nuclear division not followed immediately by cell wall formation). Walls form only after the 8-nucleate stage. Four divisions would give 16 nuclei.

options.en: Two mitotic divisions, each followed by wall formation
Three mitotic divisions, each followed by wall formation

stem.en: The region where the body of the ovule fuses with the funicle is the:

explanation.en: The hilum is the junction between the ovule and the funicle (stalk). The chalaza is the basal part opposite the micropylar end; the micropyle is the small opening at the tip of the integuments; the nucellus is the mass of cells enclosed by the integuments.

stem.en: Which of the following has an ovary with a large number of ovules?

explanation.en: The number of ovules per ovary may be one (wheat, paddy, mango) or many (papaya, watermelon, orchids). The other three options are NCERT examples of single-ovuled ovaries.

stem.en: Which pairing of plant and pistil type is correct?

explanation.en: Michelia has a multicarpellary, apocarpous gynoecium (many free carpels). Papaver (poppy) and Hibiscus have multicarpellary syncarpous (fused) pistils. So only option 2 is right.

stem.en: Which plant produces both chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers?

explanation.en: Viola (common pansy), Oxalis and Commelina produce two types of flowers: chasmogamous (open, exposed anthers and stigma) and cleistogamous (never open). Vallisneria and Zostera are water-pollinated; Yucca is moth-pollinated.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed set even in the absence of pollinators.
Reason (R): In cleistogamous flowers the anthers and stigma lie close to each other and the anthers dehisce inside the closed flower.

explanation.en: Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all. Their anthers dehisce in the closed flower and, lying close to the stigma, effect pollination. These flowers are invariably autogamous, which is exactly why seed set is assured without pollinators. R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Geitonogamy is best described as pollination that is:

explanation.en: In geitonogamy pollen goes from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. It needs a pollinating agent, so it is functionally cross-pollination, but the pollen comes from the same plant, so it is genetically similar to autogamy. Option 3 describes xenogamy; option 1 reverses the description.

options.en: Functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy
Between flowers of two different plants of the same species

stem.en: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a different plant is called:

explanation.en: Xenogamy is transfer of pollen to the stigma of a different plant; it is the only type of pollination that brings genetically different pollen to the stigma. Autogamy is within the same flower; geitonogamy between flowers of the same plant.

stem.en:
How many of the following are features of wind-pollinated flowers?
(i) Light, non-sticky pollen grains
(ii) Well-exposed stamens
(iii) Large, often feathery stigma
(iv) A single ovule in each ovary
(v) Nectar and strong fragrance
(vi) Brightly coloured petals

explanation.en: Wind-pollinated flowers have light, non-sticky pollen (i), well-exposed stamens for easy dispersal (ii), large often-feathery stigmas to trap pollen (iii), and often a single ovule per ovary with numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence (iv). Nectar, fragrance (v) and bright colours (vi) attract animals and are not needed for wind pollination. So four features.

stem.en: The 'tassels' seen on a corn cob are:

explanation.en: The tassels of the corn cob are the stigma and style, which wave in the wind to trap pollen grains, an adaptation for wind pollination.

stem.en: In which pair are both plants pollinated by water?

explanation.en: Water pollination is found in about 30 genera, mostly monocots: Vallisneria and Hydrilla in fresh water and marine sea-grasses such as Zostera. Water hyacinth and water lily are aquatic, but their flowers emerge above the water and are pollinated by insects or wind.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Not all aquatic plants use water as the agent of pollination.
Reason (R): In water hyacinth and water lily the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind.

explanation.en: In most aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind, as in land plants. That is why not all aquatic plants are water-pollinated. A is true and R explains it.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
How many of the following statements about water pollination are correct?
(i) In Vallisneria, female flowers reach the water surface on long stalks.
(ii) In Vallisneria, male flowers or pollen grains are released onto the surface of water.
(iii) In sea-grasses, female flowers stay submerged and pollen grains released into the water are long and ribbon-like.
(iv) Pollen grains of most water-pollinated species are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering.
(v) Water pollination is common in dicotyledons.

explanation.en: Statements (i)–(iv) are NCERT lines: Vallisneria female flowers reach the surface on long stalks; male flowers/pollen float on the surface and are carried passively by currents; in sea-grasses the pollen is long and ribbon-like and carried inside the water; a mucilaginous covering protects pollen from wetting. (v) is wrong: water pollination is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. So four are correct.

stem.en: The dominant biotic pollinating agents among animals are:

explanation.en: Among animals, insects, and particularly bees, are the dominant biotic pollinating agents. Birds (sunbirds, hummingbirds), bats, some primates and reptiles also pollinate but much less commonly.

stem.en: The tallest flower, about 6 feet in height, is borne by:

explanation.en: NCERT cites Amorphophallus, whose flower is about 6 feet tall, as an example of a flower that provides a safe place for insects to lay eggs. Rafflesia has the largest single flower by diameter, a different record.

stem.en:
Statement I: In Yucca, the plant and a species of moth cannot complete their life cycles without each other.
Statement II: The moth deposits its eggs in the locule of the ovary, and the flower in turn gets pollinated by the moth.

explanation.en: This is the NCERT example of mutualism in pollination. The moth deposits eggs in the locule of the ovary and pollinates the flower; the larvae come out of the eggs as the seeds start developing. Neither partner completes its life cycle without the other. Both statements are correct.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Unisexuality in which plant prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy?

explanation.en: Papaya is dioecious: male and female flowers are on different plants, so both autogamy and geitonogamy are impossible. Castor, maize and cucumber are monoecious: they bear both male and female flowers on the same plant, which prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy.

stem.en:
How many of the following discourage autogamy (self-pollination within the same flower)?
(i) Self-incompatibility
(ii) Pollen release and stigma receptivity not synchronised
(iii) Anther and stigma placed at different positions
(iv) Monoecy (as in castor and maize)
(v) Dioecy (as in papaya)
(vi) Cleistogamy

explanation.en: (i)–(iii) are the outbreeding devices NCERT lists for bisexual flowers. Unisexual flowers make autogamy impossible whether they are on the same plant (iv, monoecy, which still allows geitonogamy) or on different plants (v, dioecy). Cleistogamy (vi) ensures autogamy. So five discourage autogamy. Students often drop (iv), but monoecy prevents autogamy and fails only against geitonogamy.

stem.en: Self-incompatibility in flowering plants is:

explanation.en: Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism: the pistil recognises pollen from the same flower or plant and blocks it by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen-tube growth. Option 2 is herkogamy-type spatial separation and option 3 is dioecy. These are separate outbreeding devices.

options.en: A genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen-tube growth in the pistil
The physical separation of anther and stigma in the same flower
Production of male and female flowers on separate plants
Failure of pollen grains to form due to a defective tapetum

stem.en:
Statement I: The pistil has the ability to recognise compatible pollen and to reject incompatible pollen.
Statement II: After a compatible pollination, the pollen grain germinates on the stigma and its pollen tube grows through the tissues of the stigma and style to reach the ovary.

explanation.en: Pollen–pistil interaction is a dynamic process involving recognition followed by promotion or inhibition of the pollen, mediated by chemical components of the pollen interacting with those of the pistil. If the pollen is compatible, it germinates to produce a pollen tube through one of the germ pores, and the tube grows through the stigma and style to reach the ovary; the generative cell divides to form two male gametes if not already done. Both statements are correct.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: In an artificial hybridisation programme, emasculation is NOT needed when:

explanation.en: Emasculation is removal of anthers from a bisexual flower bud before dehiscence, so the flower cannot self-pollinate. If the female parent bears unisexual (female) flowers, there are no anthers to remove; the buds are simply bagged, and when the stigma becomes receptive they are dusted with the desired pollen and rebagged.

options.en: The female parent bears bisexual flowers
The pollen is to be stored before use
The male parent bears unisexual flowers
The female parent bears unisexual flowers

stem.en: After entering the embryo sac, the pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the:

explanation.en: The pollen tube enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus and releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of that synergid. One gamete then fuses with the egg (syngamy), and the other with the two polar nuclei in the central cell (triple fusion).

stem.en: Triple fusion in angiosperms results in the formation of the:

explanation.en: Triple fusion is the fusion of one male gamete with the two polar nuclei in the central cell, forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). The central cell becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm. The zygote comes from syngamy.

stem.en: How many nuclei in total take part in fusion during double fertilisation in a typical angiosperm?

explanation.en: Syngamy involves 2 nuclei (male gamete + egg). Triple fusion involves 3 nuclei (male gamete + 2 polar nuclei). Total = 2 + 3 = 5. Three counts only the triple fusion; four counts the two male gametes plus egg and only one polar nucleus.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In angiosperms, endosperm development precedes embryo development.
Reason (R): Endosperm cells are filled with reserve food materials used to nourish the developing embryo.

explanation.en: NCERT: 'Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Why?' The PEC divides repeatedly to form triploid endosperm tissue full of reserve food, which is used for the nutrition of the developing embryo. The embryo can develop only once this food tissue is available, so R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Tender coconut water and the surrounding white kernel represent, respectively:

explanation.en: The coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm, made of thousands of nuclei. The surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm. Coconut is NCERT's standard example of the free-nuclear-to-cellular sequence; options 1 and 3 reverse or mislabel it.

stem.en: In which seed is the endosperm completely consumed by the developing embryo before seed maturation?

explanation.en: In pea, groundnut and beans the endosperm is fully used up during embryo development (non-albuminous seeds). In castor and coconut the endosperm persists in the mature seed (albuminous); wheat, maize and barley also retain endosperm.

stem.en: In seeds of black pepper and beet, the residual persistent nucellus is called perisperm. Its ploidy is:

explanation.en: Generally the nucellus is used up, but in a few seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of it persist as perisperm. The nucellus is sporophytic tissue of the ovule, so perisperm is 2n. Endosperm, the usual food tissue, is 3n; students often mix the two up.

stem.en: The correct sequence of stages in the development of a dicot embryo is:

explanation.en: The zygote, at the micropylar end of the embryo sac, gives rise to the proembryo and then to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo. The heart shape appears when the two cotyledon primordia start to grow, which comes after the globular stage.

stem.en: In a grass embryo, the coleoptile is:

explanation.en: In the grass family the cotyledon is called the scutellum and is placed laterally. The epicotyl has a shoot apex and a few leaf primordia enclosed in a hollow foliar structure, the coleoptile. The radicle and root cap are enclosed by the coleorhiza. Option 1 is the scutellum, option 3 the coleorhiza.

options.en: A hollow foliar structure enclosing the shoot apex and a few leaf primordia
An undifferentiated sheath enclosing the radicle and root cap
The portion of the embryonal axis below the cotyledon

stem.en:
Match column I with column II:
A. Scutellum
B. Coleorhiza
C. Epicotyl
D. Hypocotyl
I. Portion of the embryonal axis below the level of the cotyledons
II. Undifferentiated sheath enclosing the radicle and root cap
III. Single cotyledon of the grass embryo
IV. Portion of the embryonal axis above the level of the cotyledons

explanation.en: Scutellum = cotyledon of grasses (III). Coleorhiza = sheath around radicle and root cap (II). Epicotyl = part of the axis above the cotyledons, ending in the plumule (IV). Hypocotyl = part below the cotyledons, ending in the radicle (I). Option 2 swaps epicotyl and hypocotyl, the usual slip.

stem.en: Which of the following post-fertilisation changes is correctly matched?

explanation.en: After fertilisation the ovule develops into the seed and the ovary into the fruit. The integuments form the seed coat (testa and tegmen), the ovary wall forms the pericarp, the zygote forms the embryo and the PEN forms the endosperm. Options 1 and 2 swap pericarp and seed coat.

stem.en: Which statement about seeds is INCORRECT?

explanation.en: Options 1–3 are NCERT facts: seeds dry to 10–15% moisture and become dormant; the lupine record (~10,000 years) and the 2000-year-old Phoenix dactylifera seed show how long seeds can stay viable. Option 4 is wrong: parasitic plants such as Orobanche and Striga produce thousands of tiny seeds per fruit, as do some orchids.

options.en: A mature seed generally has only 10–15 per cent moisture by mass
Seeds of Lupinus arcticus from the Arctic Tundra germinated after an estimated 10,000 years of dormancy
A 2000-year-old viable seed of the date palm was recovered from King Herod's palace near the Dead Sea
Seeds of Orobanche and Striga are large and few in number per fruit

stem.en:
Statement I: In apple, strawberry and cashew, the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation, so these are called false fruits.
Statement II: Parthenocarpic fruits such as banana develop without fertilisation and can be induced by applying growth hormones.

explanation.en: Both are NCERT facts. In most plants the fruit develops only from the ovary (true fruit), but in apple, strawberry and cashew the thalamus also contributes, so they are false fruits. Parthenocarpic fruits develop without fertilisation and are seedless; banana is the example, and parthenocarpy can be induced with growth hormones.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Banana is an example of a fruit that develops without fertilisation. Such fruits are called:

explanation.en: Fruits that develop without fertilisation are parthenocarpic; they are seedless, and banana is the classic example. Apomixis forms seeds without fertilisation, which is a different process. False fruits involve the thalamus.

stem.en:
How many of the following statements about apomixis are correct?
(i) Apomixis is the production of seeds without fertilisation.
(ii) It is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction.
(iii) It is found in some species of Asteraceae and grasses.
(iv) Nucellar cells protruding into the embryo sac can form embryos, as in many Citrus and mango varieties.
(v) Apomictic hybrid seeds show segregation of characters in the progeny, so they must be bought every year.

explanation.en: (i)–(iv) are correct NCERT lines. In some species the diploid egg cell forms without reduction division and develops into an embryo without fertilisation; in others (Citrus, mango) nucellar cells grow into the embryo sac and form embryos, giving polyembryony. (v) is wrong: ordinary hybrid seeds segregate, so farmers must buy them every year. Apomictic hybrid seed shows no segregation, so farmers could keep using it. That is why breeders want apomixis genes in hybrids. Four correct.
